summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of severe Crohn’s disease, status post subtotal colectomy and ileorectal anastomosis, was admitted for a flare characterized by severe left lower quadrant abdominal pain and frequent watery diarrhea—up to 40 episodes per day. He was initially kept NPO, started on IV fluids and IV steroids, and managed with pain control. Stool studies were negative for infectious causes. He gradually improved, tolerating a clear liquid diet and advancing to low-residue foods, with reduced pain and bowel frequency. He was transitioned to oral prednisone 60 mg daily and discharged home with instructions to follow up with his gastroenterologist for steroid tapering. His GERD was managed with omeprazole, and he was also discharged with loperamide, pain medication, and continued B12 injections.
problems: Regional enteritis of small intestine with large intestine
